registered.new: An acceptance is a manifestation of assent to the offer's terms; the offeror is “master of the offer” and may define what qualifies. Acceptance must be on the same terms and unconditional, may be by promise or by performance, and silence ordinarily is not acceptance. It is effective on dispatch by reasonable means (except for options), and notification of acceptance by promise is ordinarily required. Legal qualification: under Restatement § 63, an acceptance takes effect on dispatch only if it is made in a manner and by a medium the offer invites and the offer does not provide otherwise; an acceptance by an uninvited medium ordinarily takes effect only on receipt (C&M 262; § 67), one under an option only on receipt (§ 63(b)), and rejections and revocations take effect on receipt (§§ 40, 42). new.label: Acceptance by a medium the offer did not invite
new.detail: First ask whether the medium was in fact invited: unless the language or circumstances indicate otherwise, an offer invites acceptance by any medium reasonable in the circumstances, such as the one the offeror used or one customary in similar transactions (Restatement §§ 30(2), 65). An acceptance by a medium not invited does not get the dispatch rule of § 63(a): a mailed acceptance of an offer made by telegram ordinarily takes effect only on receipt (C&M 262). Under § 67, a seasonably sent acceptance by an uninvited means is still treated as operative on dispatch if it arrives within the time a properly sent acceptance would normally have taken. Compare that effective time with the time any revocation or rejection was received (§§ 40, 42).

new.detail: Under § 54(2) the performance was an acceptance.
